newsitem.title: ESTONIA: USAID quits Estonia as it no longer needs support.
newsitem.headline: USAID quits Estonia as it no longer needs support.

text.p: The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) on Monday said it was to end its assistance to Estonia as the Baltic state no longer needed its support.
Estonia, which broke from the former Soviet Union in 1991, was the first former Communist-bloc state where the USAID has ended its assistance programme. It will finish at the end of this month.

"The rapid progress that Estonia has made in re-establishing its democratic institutions and economic relations with the West makes it the first of the central European countries to 'graduate' from U.S. assistance," USAID said in a statement.
USAID has launched more than 60 projects and injected some $30 million into the country, regarded as one of eastern Europe's most successful reformers.
USAID supported the re-establishment of democracy in Estonia and promoted economic reform and environment protection.

"From a country that unilaterally needed help, Estonia has become a state that wants to be, and can be, a partner in international cooperation," President Lennart Meri told a ceremony marking Estonia's graduation from USAID programmes.
